title: Sparse polynomial threshold representation
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for its Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq[n]$, and set $s=\lceil 4n(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|)^2\rceil$. Then $f$ has a polynomial threshold representation with at most $s$ nonzero Walsh coefficients, and it is also the threshold sign of a sum of exactly $s$ signed Walsh characters, allowing repeated characters.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n>0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and set $L=\sum_S|\widehat f(S)|$ and $s=\lceil4nL^2\rceil$.
There exists a real multilinear polynomial $p(x)=\sum_Sa_S\chi_S(x)$ with at most $s$ nonzero coefficients such that $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
Moreover, there exist subsets $S_1,\ldots,S_s\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with repetitions allowed, and signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_s\in\{-1,1\}$ such that
\[
 f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}\left(\sum_{j=1}^s\varepsilon_j\chi_{S_j}(x)\right)
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\{0,1\}^n.
\]
